reviews.text:
There were no problems with the examination or treatment itself, and I appreciated being able to choose a doctor.

However, I felt uneasy and distrustful because a staff member's child repeatedly opened the examination room door during the examination, and also regarding the safety management of the back area where pets are taken.

I have doubts about the level of care and professionalism expected in a medical setting, so I will refrain from using their services again in the future.

I previously had my degu treated here.
First of all, the nurse was very gentle, quick, and skilled at handling the animal. The doctor was also young and explained things flexibly, including recent cases, which was very helpful.

They provide thorough health checkups and examine everything carefully. They also perform CT scans skillfully without anesthesia.

The clinic is clean and tidy, and I felt the love and care they put into treating animals.

I think everyone has their own opinions, but I believe these are opinions that come from people who cherish their pets, so there may be good and bad doctors.

Around June 2026, I searched for a vet in Osaka City for treatment of my turtle and took it to this clinic.

I don't want to give a low rating, but I'm doing so for the sake of the animal. I don't want other pet owners to go through the same thing. I haven't had any other reptiles or small animals examined by this vet, so I can't comment on their skills in treating animals other than turtles. This evaluation is solely based on the turtle examination. I won't mention the vet's name because you can find out which vet I'm talking about by looking at their website. The vet's diagnosis was no different from an AI's, leaving me with nothing but distrust and questioning the purpose of face-to-face medical care. They only said the illness was caused by problems with the living environment. No matter how many times I explained the living environment and told them that it wasn't the case, they wouldn't listen. Unlike humans, animals can't speak, so shouldn't a doctor consider the causes and possibilities of illness that ordinary people wouldn't know about? The only thing the vet did was weigh the turtle. No medication, treatment, or tests were performed. Only a prescription was given. Of course, there was no visual inspection of the oral cavity, which an ordinary person would be too afraid to do. I strongly felt that the vet's skills and understanding were lacking. I was told to come back in a week if there was no improvement in the symptoms, but I don't want to deal with this anymore. I plan to take my child to another clinic. If this is the doctor's diagnosis, I don't even want to think about why he can't prescribe medication when the AI ​​says the symptoms will dramatically improve with the doctor's prescription.

This doctor is incompetent.
I took my reptile there. I called to inquire about the species and symptoms, and they said they had a specialist veterinarian who could examine it. However, the veterinarian was an amateur and didn't perform any examination or treatment, simply saying "I can't see it," and only prescribed antibiotics, charging me 8000 yen. The medication had absolutely no effect. It was a complete waste of time and money.
If they lacked the knowledge and experience, they should have refused over the phone. (This is a tactic where they claim to be able to treat anything to get people to come to the hospital and then charge exorbitant fees.)
I'll say it again: This doctor is incompetent.

I'm very grateful that you took care of my dog ​​while I was traveling. I feel very safe knowing that you have a medical system in place if anything happens. Thank you for your continued support. m(__)m
This is my second visit, and the doctor and staff are both very kind and attentive. It's a great help that they offer reptile care, as there aren't many hospitals that treat reptiles.

My dog's gums are weak, so I asked them to brush his teeth, which absolutely needs brushing. When I got home, there was still food in his teeth. They only took the cost of the toothbrush, but they didn't actually brush his teeth. It's awful. They returned the blanket I'd left him with with poop still on it. What's more, they let him sit on the blanket after shampooing him. I really can't trust what they're feeling. I left my dog ​​in a VIP room, but it was expensive and the service was awful. I seriously doubt they're really a facility for dogs, and whether they understand the owners' feelings. I wouldn't leave my dog ​​in a hotel like that again. Don't lie to me!
As for the hospital visits, they can't provide any life-saving treatments for dogs. They can only provide simple treatments. It would be putting your precious dog's life at risk. I strongly recommend another hospital. Last year, my dog ​​went here for six months, but his condition never improved and only got worse. He died in agony without even being diagnosed. The only medication they gave me was an anti-diarrheal medication. I was shocked when the director finally told me he wasn't a specialist. If that's the case, why didn't they tell me earlier that they couldn't cure him? They could have found another hospital. The director insisted that I keep going to the hospital every day for IV drips. Daily IV drips can be fatal for a dog with a heart condition! Back then, I was ignorant, so I just followed the director's orders every day. Even the director had little knowledge of how to administer medication, so they were groping around in the dark. He avoided risky examinations that required anesthesia, and on the day of a CT scan that required anesthesia, the director refused due to mysterious abdominal pain. He didn't perform any tests after that.

After my dog ​​died, I was surprised to hear from the groomer that the director had said that something I had fed him had caused his death. In the end, we never found out the cause of death. Of course, they didn't perform any tests that could have revealed the cause, like a CT scan that required anesthesia. They told me from the beginning until the very end that the cause was unknown, but within the hospital, they blamed me for his death, even the groomer. Everyone thought I had caused his death, and I was sad. I truly cannot forgive this director. How can he say such a thing? I'm deeply hurt, and I realize he's the kind of person who always blames others for everything. I was wrong to entrust his care to such a person. But time cannot be turned back.

My other dog, who is still alive, recently became near death, and after much searching, I found another hospital. He's a 12-year-old Chihuahua with a heart condition, but they properly anesthetized him, examined him, diagnosed his illness, and he recovered in two months.

At the end of the year, all the daycare centers were full, so I had no choice but to admit him to the hospital, thinking they would at least do what I asked them to do. However, they stopped giving him the medication I had requested, and they gave him one bottle of special liquid food that had to be consumed within 48 hours for six days. The amount was so small that it essentially didn't do anything. The doctor in charge knew about this, but he didn't tell me anything, and he didn't give me any explanation or progress reports.

When I went to pick him up, there was no explanation at all, and I received a reply not from a doctor or nurse, but from the groomer. Was this intentional? This is a cover-up. My dog ​​was on the brink of death, but at a delicate stage in his health, having somehow managed to recover at another hospital, they wouldn't even prescribe his medication. They fed him food that had already expired, and even though I explained the expiration date to them multiple times before leaving him, no one noticed that it had expired for six days. I deeply regret leaving my beloved dog in such a horrible place.
I've heard from other pet owners that their dogs didn't improve at this hospital, and instead got worse, and received completely different diagnoses than those from several other hospitals, making them untrustworthy. I wholeheartedly agree. The communication between doctors, nurses, and pet groomers is complicated and completely untrustworthy. There are far too many facts to list here. I sincerely warn everyone who reads this post. To save your dog's life, please find another hospital. You're only putting your dog's life at risk. The people here are not doctors. They are ignorant, showy, and bluffing, but they have no sincerity whatsoever. I was fooled and completely trusted them. If I had been able to see my previous self and warn him, I'm sure my dog ​​could have been saved at another hospital before his condition worsened, and he might still be by my side today. I'm truly, truly regretful. It's too late to regret now. Other hospitals have specialized knowledge and experienced doctors. Saving a dog's life depends on the owner's accurate judgment. I strongly recommend researching your dog's health online, identifying the relevant illness, and having him examined by a specialist in cardiology, arthrology, ophthalmology, etc. There's a big difference between a local doctor and a specialist. My beloved dog, who lived the longest until the very end, had heart problems since he was a puppy and had been treated by a cardiologist ever since. The medication he received worked wonders, and he was so healthy that they said he wouldn't die from heart disease. Although his heart was in poor condition, his blood pressure numbers were maintained without any serious deterioration. I learned my lesson at Central Animal Hospital, so I strongly believe that choosing the right hospital and having him examined by a specialist would have saved my dog.

The waiting room has a stylish atmosphere with a black and white color scheme.
However, the waiting time on weekends is... ⤵️
Nevertheless, I'm grateful that the doctor is very kind and attentive during examinations. ☺️

I've been there a few times with my bird, but they've never helped me.
It's fine to go for small errands, but if my bird gets sick I won't be able to get any help.
There is a hospital in Osaka that specializes in birds, so if your bird gets sick, make sure you take it there!

I believe this is a profit-driven animal hospital.
I wouldn't even give it one star.
I changed hospitals due to moving, and since the cause was already known from blood tests and examinations, I only wanted medication. I brought the test results from the previous hospital with me, but they said they couldn't prescribe medication because they couldn't determine the cause from that alone. Since it would be a hassle to go home and bring back the examination records, I asked them to do only the necessary blood tests. However, they ended up doing a heart test that I hadn't requested, and without prior confirmation, I was charged approximately 33,000 yen. I seriously question the character of a doctor who can charge this much when it's a first visit and I only wanted medication.

The doctor was Dr. Hosoi, and he was very intimidating. Incidentally, I had previously explained that my cat was elderly and that I would be managing it with medication, and that I didn't want to burden her with unnecessary tests.

Now I've switched to a different hospital, and I've found a good doctor who carefully considered my budget and how far I wanted to go with future treatment.

That's why I wanted to leave this review – because this hospital is very dangerous – and I wanted to warn others to be careful.

Bring my dogs without appointment, but they accept and I was able to talk to the veterinarian and got the medication for my dogs. Stuff is friendly and the doctor is patient for listening and explaining.

When my rabbit was four years old,
he lost his appetite and his tears wouldn't stop, so I took him to the doctor.
He discovered that his upper teeth had grown upward, affecting his nose and eyes, causing the tears.

He suggested a nasolacrimal duct irrigation,
but said that would require general anesthesia.
He had heard that giving rabbits general anesthesia is very dangerous, so he said it would be better to just wait and see if his condition worsened.

I wasn't convinced, so I asked around with my acquaintances, and the first one was a veterinary hospital in Nishinagahori. The doctor there, who also owns rabbits, was very sympathetic, but ultimately said he would need general anesthesia.

I continued to consult with friends and word of mouth,
and was recommended a veterinary hospital in Ibaraki City, so I transferred him there.

He performed a nasolacrimal duct irrigation on the same day in a short amount of time without anesthesia. He also said that his rabbit's sharp teeth had caused canker sores in his mouth, which had reduced his appetite, so he filed down the sharp parts without anesthesia.

About once a month, his teeth would sharpen and his appetite would decrease, but
thanks to continuing this emergency treatment, he lived to be 9 years old.
He eventually passed away after about three days of difficulty breathing, apparently due to a tumor in his lungs. I think he lived a very long life among rabbits whose teeth deteriorated early.

This veterinary hospital has a prestigious name, so I rushed there thinking I would feel safe, but in the end I was glad I didn't end up going there.

It may be a good place to treat dogs and cats,

I thought it was very dangerous that anesthesia was the first option, so I gave it an honest review. I hope this is helpful for people who keep small animals.
There are some female doctors who seem completely heartless and it's really off-putting.

This is an excellent hospital that treats both people and cats with great kindness and care.

My cat required equipment that only two animal hospitals in all of Osaka Prefecture have, but even then, they referred me to another hospital, handed over the case to the other veterinarian, and compiled the test results.

This is a wonderful hospital that puts the well-being of pets, who are family members, first and foremost, providing explanations and treatment suggestions accordingly.

May 21st Update:
The hospital we were transferred to had advanced medical equipment that only a few in the prefecture possess, but I felt that the doctors' care at Chuo Animal Medical Center was superior.

Chuo Animal Medical Center provides thorough explanations, takes the time to carefully examine animals, and treats them as family.

At the hospital we transferred to due to the availability of specialized equipment, the doctor called me "owner," but at Chuo Animal Medical Center, they called me "mother," and they took the time to provide more thorough explanations and discuss treatment plans in detail.

Because it was a rare symptom, I was anxious and researched many other hospitals, but Chuo Hospital has above-average facilities, and above all, the doctor's approach was kind. For my timid family, I felt that Chuo Hospital was the better choice.

As you'll understand if you visit other hospitals, I think it's an excellent hospital where medical facilities and the warmth of the staff are combined at a high level.

My Java sparrow was in a very critical condition due to air sac inflammation.

Thank you for your prompt and accurate response.

It has recovered completely.

Thank you to the veterinarian and staff.

I had been going to this hospital for a long time, but I began to question their attitude and the treatment they provided, as well as their condescending attitude. I also began to have doubts about their treatment plan, so I moved to another hospital for a second opinion.

They had been treating me for suspected heart disease for several years, but when I went to a cardiologist in Hokusetsu, Osaka, they said it was definitely not heart disease at all. The medication I had been giving them reluctantly was also completely unnecessary at this stage.

It also seems this hospital is in contact with my insurance company, and they explained to me that it was heart disease without my consent, and I wasn't even covered by insurance, which is the worst.

I spent so much money on a misdiagnosis, threw away all my money, and caused so much pain to my precious family, so I will never go there again.

If you want to make your precious family go through that, then please go. I will not forgive you.

The interior was clean overall, and the receptionist was quick and polite.

I would like to use this service again.

There's a bit of a wait, but it's a wonderful hospital that also treats tortoises.
There aren't many places that treat tortoises, you know!

I've been taking my two sugar gliders and budgie to this clinic because they also treat exotic animals.

My male sugar glider has had several issues, including penis prolapse and leg dislocations, and they've always treated him very carefully.

I've been using this clinic for the treatment of exotic animals and birds. It's a great help because there aren't many other places that treat them.

For a while, the evening consultation hours were only until 6 PM on weekdays, which made it difficult to use, but when I checked recently and decided to go, I found that they've returned to 7 PM. Also, it seems that the head veterinarian and staff have changed quite a bit.
When the head veterinarian specializing in reptiles was still there, the waiting times were so long it was exhausting, but now it's relatively calm, so the waiting pain is gone. …

He seems to have great confidence in his work with exotic animals, but I can't expect much from him when it comes to budgies. When I visited him on another day after he was diagnosed with testicular tumor, he said, "Your legs might be …

I took my one-year-old corn snake with me.
It had been refusing to eat, but it was only two weeks old.
It passed away the night after it was given an injection at the hospital. …
